newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Brief power outage could cost Taiwan firms $14 mln.
newsitem.headline: Brief power outage could cost Taiwan firms $14 mln.

text.p: A two-minute power failure at a southern Taiwan industrial park on Thursday was expected to cost affected firms T$400 million (US$14 million) or more in losses, local media reported.

The morning blip at Jenta Industrial Park in Kaohsiung forced giant Chinese Petroleum Corp to shut down its No.5 naphtha cracker as well as a score of related petroleum and chemical plants, the state oil monopoly said by telephone.
Officials at electrical utility Taiwan Power Co, which supplies the Jenta park, said the outage lasted about two minutes, but were at a loss to explain the failure.

The United Evening News said other prominent victims were Formosa Plastics Group members Formosa Plastics Corp and Nan Ya Plastics Corp as well as China Petrochem Corp, Grand Petrochem Corp, USI Far East Corp and China Manmade Corp.
All were forced to shut down part or all of their facilities in and around the park, the newspaper said.
The newspaper quoted unidentified sources as calculating total production and related losses at T$400 million or more.
No official estimates of damage or losses were available.

Chinese Petroleum executives said the power failure forced them to shut down a score of plants at Jenta, including the company's No.5 cracker, which has annual production capacity of 400,000 tonnes of ethylene.
The monopoly's facilities were being brought slowly back on line and operations would be back to normal by Saturday, they said, declining to estimate losses.
